## Conventions

- `!!` marks something I got wrong at least once or want to remember.
- Worked examples follow the same pattern: **Question** → **Pseudocode** → code → **Answer**.
- Every code chunk uses the native pipe `|>` and `<-` for assignment (see [Assignment Operators](workflow.qmd#assignment-operators)).
- Packages: `tidyverse` (dplyr, ggplot2, tidyr, readr, stringr, lubridate) and `nycflights13` (the `flights` data). `mpg` comes with ggplot2. Newer chapters also use `infer`, `rvest`, `janitor` and `knitr`.

## Useful Resources {#useful-resources}

| Resource | What it's good for |
|:------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------------|
| [R for Data Science (2e)](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/) | The main tidyverse reference: [joins](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/joins.html), [logical vectors and `%in%`](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/logicals.html), [web scraping](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/webscraping.html) |
| [Introduction to Modern Statistics](https://openintro-ims.netlify.app/foundations-randomization.html) | Hypothesis testing by randomization (our course textbook) |
| [infer package](https://infer.tidymodels.org/) | Simulation-based tests in R |
| [rvest](https://rvest.tidyverse.org/) and [SelectorGadget guide](https://rvest.tidyverse.org/articles/selectorgadget.html) | Scraping tables and finding selectors |
| [An Introduction to Statistical Learning](https://www.statlearning.com/) | k-NN, training vs. testing, overfitting (free PDF) |
| [Posit cheatsheets: dplyr](https://rstudio.github.io/cheatsheets/html/data-transformation.html) | One-page dplyr reference |
| [Quarto: caching](https://quarto.org/docs/computations/caching.html) | `cache: true` and when chunks rerun |
